# Lionheart Fixt 0.24.0 - The Register

0.23.0 spent a release making the Knights of Saladin worth joining, and earned a fair objection: nothing
in this game should be only a benefit. By then that allegiance was the purest upside in it.

So all five were audited.

## What each allegiance actually costs you

| allegiance | the bill, before this release |
|---|---|
| Inquisitor | +25% at the Barcelona herbalist, **+50%** at the Montaillou weird woman, +10% at the rogue in the Plains; the Cathars, the shepherd and the witch all withhold |
| Wielder | the Montaillou mayor, Beatrice, the Crypt captains |
| Templar | +25% at the herbalist. **That was the entire list** |
| Goblin Horde | the Montaillou guard's hand never leaving his hilt |
| Knights of Saladin | **nothing at all** |

Every one of the Order of Saladin's 42 checks is a welcome, a thanks, or a piece of information. Nothing
anywhere charged it, refused it, or watched it.

Each of the three now costs something -- and in every case the grievance was already written into the
game, sitting a few rooms away from the character who should have been holding it.

## The Order gets a name in the book

The Bishop of Pamiers is in Montaillou doing exactly one thing, which the gate guard describes precisely:
*"a man with a book, asking questions, and every soul in Montaillou answering him one at a time."* He
lets you introduce yourself as a Knight Templar or as an Inquisitor. There was never a third option.

Now there is, and the introduction is the price:

> *"A Knight of Saladin. <He does not look up. The quill keeps moving.> The Temple vouches for your order,
> so I will not have you stopped at the gate. You will forgive an old man his thoroughness, though: a
> sworn brother of an order named for a Saracen sultan, arriving in a village I am in the middle of
> emptying of heretics, in the same week. There. You are written down. Now - what was it you wanted?"*

After which the gate guard who used to call you an ally of the Temple stops being pleased about it:

> *"Aye. His grace named your order to us this week, and he does not trouble to name orders he has no use
> for. You are an ally of the Temple and you may pass - I am not the man who decides otherwise. Do your
> business in the daylight, and be seen doing it."*

The gate does not close. Vanilla states the alliance outright and this does not argue with it. You lose
the warmth, and only if you choose to say who you are.

## The Temple pays for its board

The Cathar toughs in the Montaillou tavern pick their fight over one grievance: *"it isn't enough you and
your priest friends eat our food and tax our farms?"* Three rooms away, in the mayor's house, the Templar
knights are working through Pierre's larder by right of the code -- *"Bring more food! And more ale!"*,
*"You must provide food and shelter to any knight who asks for aid."*

A Knight Templar in that tavern is the man they are complaining about, and the tree never noticed. He
could use the same line everyone else uses -- *"I'm not a priest, nor are they my friends"* -- which is
true and beside the point. He can't now:

> *"Not a priest. Worse. You are one of the knights who sleeps in Pierre's house and eats what is in it
> and calls it his right by the code. Your lot went through my brother's winter stores in three days and
> left him a blessing for them. So. What is a winter worth, brother?"*

150 gold, or the brawl. It takes nothing from a Templar except the ability to pretend.

## The Horde pays for the carts

Sworn goblins already buy from the warren vendor at 0.75 where everyone else pays 1. Nothing charged the
other way -- and the Montaillou guard says why it should: *"We have had word of what the Horde did at the
Crossroads."*

The Crossroads is a real map with four merchants standing on it. Alvaro sold there at a flat rate to
anybody, though vanilla already has him sorting beggars by race, so he is hardly short of opinions:

> *"Si. I sell to you. I sell to everyone, amigo, that is the business. But last spring your Khan's boys
> came through this crossroads and took what they liked off three of my carts and left me the axles, and
> somebody has to pay for the carts."*

**1.5** -- the steepest surcharge in the game, matching what the weird woman charges an Inquisitor. Both
his shop nodes are gated, the high-karma one included, because that store exists on the strength of
*"word of your good deeds"* and the same ears heard about the Crossroads.

## One measurement retracted

The first pass at this counted `X NOT` requirement gates as "costs of being X". That is wrong: almost all
of them are replies like *"I would like to know more about the Knights Templar"* -- offered to people who
are **not** members. On that bad metric the Temple and the Horde looked more lopsided than the Order of
Saladin, which had the reverse of the truth.

**Fixt** is a cumulative restoration-and-repair mod for Lionheart, after Fallout Fixt.

Download, unzip, run `Mod Manager.bat`. Needs a character who has **not yet entered Montaillou's church or
hamlet**, and for the Crossroads, one who has not yet met Alvaro. Unplayed; what you find goes into
0.24.1.
